subject: Workplace Skills
title: Leaders Versus Managers
description: A 60-second lesson on Leaders Versus Managers.

hook.text: Peter Drucker said managers do things right, but leaders do the right things. The distinction changes everything.

buildup.text: Managers maintain systems, hit targets, and enforce process. Leaders set direction, inspire, and navigate ambiguity.

discovery.text: You can manage without leading and lead without managing. The best professionals learn to do both.

twist.text: Leadership isn't a title. The intern who rallies the team around a vision is leading; the VP reading scripts is not.

climax.text: Ask yourself: am I optimizing existing paths or creating new ones? The answer reveals whether you're managing.

punchline.text: Lead by choosing direction. Manage by running the path.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between leaders and managers?
options: Leaders have higher titles than managers
Managers maintain systems while leaders set direction and navigate ambiguity
Leaders focus on strategy while managers focus on people
